how_to_read_the_bpw_column.warning: These complete-BPW figures are NOT comparable to the 0.9774 of Math-Preserve and must not be quoted as if they were.
how_to_read_the_bpw_column.why: The fixture is 64x64 = 4,096 weights. Fixed costs -- headers, codebooks, island indices -- do not shrink with the tensor, so at this size they dominate. A2 reads 21.0 BPW because its residual is stored at float16 over a tiny matrix; on a real tensor the codebooks amortize across orders of magnitude more rows.
how_to_read_the_bpw_column.what_the_column_IS_good_for: proving that each arm's accounting reconciles exactly -- sum(components) == total_bytes -- which is the property the one-bit law is measured with. All five packing arms reconcile.
how_to_read_the_bpw_column.what_it_is_NOT_good_for: ranking the arms. Ranking happens on a real parent under the preregistered gates, and weight-space error is inadmissible there.
